Start a new detector in this repository
Do not copy an existing detector by hand. Generate the skeleton from a checkout of this repository:

npm ci
npm run build
node dist/src/cli.js new-detector go-modules --ecosystem go
The id is the detector's stable identifier (lowercase letters, digits, and single hyphens, starting with a letter).

A detector is named by the first segment of its rule ids. Conformance is the shared harness: determinism, locations, evidence, a mandatory zero-finding fixture, and malformed input that does not throw. "Repositories with findings" counts corpus repositories with at least one expected finding for that detector. "Zero-finding repositories" counts corpus repositories of the detector's ecosystem with no expected findings. A repository is blind when a rule fixed before the scan chose it. The built-in GitHub Actions detector uses this metadata for full 40-character commit pins it cannot resolve. It classifies a covered action from a valid trailing version comment first, or from Offing's bundled exact SHA-to-release map when no comment is present. An unknown SHA is reported with reason
; a present but unusable comment is reported with reason
. Neither case becomes a lifecycle finding because Offing does not guess a release line.
This resolution is fully offline. The bundled map is reviewed and regenerated by a separate maintainer tool; repository scans never query GitHub or another service.
